text: Hello, this is an automated message from your courier service. Your parcel could not be delivered because of an incomplete address. Press one to speak to our customer care executive.
tell: Robocall about a parcel you may not be expecting, routing you to a live 'executive' who controls the next step.

text: Good morning madam, I am calling from the international courier hub in Mumbai. A package sent under your name to Iran has been held at our facility. Did you book this shipment?
tell: Opens with a parcel you never sent, so the denial itself becomes the lever for the next stage.

text: Sir, your Speed Post consignment is stuck at the sorting centre because customs duty is pending. If it is not cleared today, the parcel will be returned to the sender.
tell: Duty demanded by an unsolicited phone call rather than on the delivery notice or official tracking page.

text: Customs officers opened the package and found five passports, three credit cards and one hundred forty grams of MDMA. This is a serious offence under the NDPS Act.
tell: Contraband contents are invented to create fear; customs does not phone a named 'sender' with a list of seized items.

text: I am Customs Superintendent Nair from the air cargo complex. The parcel is registered against your Aadhaar and phone number, so legally you are the sender unless you give a statement now.
tell: Claims your ID makes you legally liable on the spot, a false premise that forces you to 'clear your name' by phone.

text: Our tracking record shows the booking was paid with a card in your name. I will give you a complaint reference number, and you can confirm it on the website link I am sending you by SMS.
tell: Self-verification through a link the caller supplies proves nothing; verify only via the courier's official site you type yourself.

text: Please do not discuss this parcel with family members until your statement is recorded. If the real sender is someone known to you, they may destroy the evidence.
tell: Secrecy framed as protecting the investigation; it actually prevents anyone from telling you it is a scam.

text: Stay on this line while I transfer you to the customs cyber desk. If the call disconnects, the system automatically marks you as absconding.
tell: No system flags you as a fugitive for hanging up; the threat exists to keep you on the line.

text: Move to a quiet room where nobody can overhear you. This is a confidential customs matter and third parties are not permitted to be present on the call.
tell: Physically separating you from others removes the person most likely to stop the payment.

text: The parcel will be handed over to the police at six this evening. After that the case cannot be closed from the customs side and a warrant will be issued in your name.
tell: Artificial handover deadline converts a parcel problem into an imminent arrest.

text: The clearance window closes in one hour. If the duty is not paid now, a penalty of ten times the value is added and your address is blacklisted for international shipping.
tell: Invented multipliers and blacklists; real duty notices give days, a written demand and official payment channels.

text: Your consignment is already on the list for destruction tomorrow morning. Only a clearance done right now during this call can release it.
tell: 'Only during this call' removes the option to verify independently later.

text: Pay the customs clearance fee of eighteen thousand five hundred rupees to the UPI ID I am sending. The moment the payment reflects, I will release the parcel and cancel the complaint.
tell: Government duty is never collected to a personal UPI ID given out by a caller.

text: Scan the QR code I sent on WhatsApp and enter your UPI PIN to complete the duty payment. You will get a receipt from the customs department within ten minutes.
tell: Entering a UPI PIN always sends money out of your account; it is never needed to receive or clear anything.

text: To file the no objection certificate I need your card number, the expiry date and the three digit code on the back. A processing fee of ninety-nine rupees will be deducted from it.
tell: A tiny fee is the pretext for capturing full card details, which are then used for much larger charges.
